items.title: Legendary Bushra Ansari brings one-woman show to Mississauga
items.summary: Legendary Pakistani entertainer Bushra Ansari is bringing her one-woman performance to Mississauga. Shaam-e-Tabassum (translated as evening of smile) comes to Meadowvale Theatre in Mississauga on Sept. 5. The show, a mix of comedy, storytelling, satire and music, is in Canada for the first time. com that the performance will be in Urdu with a little Punjabi. “The humour I’m going to create is around our culture, our language,” she said. Ansari, 70, started her career at the age of nine and became part of the golden era of Pakistani television. “I started as a singer, then I acted and I did comedy,” she said. Ansari is well known in Pakistan and has won numerous awards during her career, including the Presidential Pride of Performance Award in 1989 for her contributions to Pakistani television. She now lives in Richmond Hill, but continues to travel to Pakistan for work. She has also worked in Canadian television, starring as Mommy Ji in the series Our Big Punjabi Family. In 2023, after decades of success on television, Ansari took an unexpected risk: she stepped onto the stage alone in her first one-woman show, Malika-e-Tabassum (queen of smiles). The show sold out the 20 performances and packed houses across Pakistan. Ansari explored relationships, culture, feminism and the absurdities of everyday life.

items.title: Square One is giving away gift cards to shoppers and their guests
items.summary: Square One is giving Mississauga locals another reason to bring their out-of-town guests, friends and family to the Mississauga shopping centre, with a free gift card and luxurious gift. Happening now until Sept. 7, 2026, you’ll score a $25 Square One gift card when you bring a guest (or guests) from outside Mississauga to the shopping centre’s Guest Experience desk, located on Level 2 near Wilfred. On top of that, accompanying guests will receive a six-piece box of chocolates courtesy of Purdys Chocolatier at Square One, the popular Canadian chocolate brand known for their decadent chocolates, indulgent flavours and innovative new creations. It’s Square One’s way of saying thank you for including the major shopping centre in your travel plans. To qualify, the host must be a Mississauga resident and must be accompanied by at least one guest aged 18+ who resides more than 65 km from Square One (valid ID required for both host and guest). The full terms and conditions are listed here. Square One remains one of Mississauga’s most popular travel spots for out-of-towners visiting the city. Known as the biggest shopping centre in Ontario, the mall is home to over 330 retailers, making it a one-stop destination for all things fashion, beauty, dining, and lifestyle. When it’s time to relax and grab a bite to eat, over 100 places to eat – both inside the main shopping centre and at The Food District, Square One’s curated food hall – cover any craving with a wide range of sweet treats and savoury cuisines from around the world. The Food District features both mainstays offering dine-in and takeout options, as well as a rotating selection of pop-ups offering up something new and delicious to try, so for the adventurous foodie it’s worth visiting often.

Members of the Marine Unit, along with several uniform officers, attended the scene. Peel Regional Paramedic Services and the fire department also responded as a precaution. items.title: Arts and community organizations are invited to apply for Mississauga’s 2027 Community and Culture Grant Programs
items.summary: Funding is available for organizations of all sizes; interested applicants are encouraged to attend a virtual information webinar. Not-for-profit organizations in Mississauga seeking financial support for the 2027 calendar year are encouraged to begin the application process for the City of Mississauga’s Culture and Community Grant Programs. Funding is available for organizations of all sizes, including small and grassroots groups that enhance and expand recreational opportunities, local events, arts programming, and other community initiatives in Mississauga. Organizations interested in applying to a grant program are encouraged to review the grant guidelines and attend one of the applicable virtual information webinars being held in September. Not-for-profit community groups can apply for the following grants: Grant funding for this program supports emerging and established, not-for-profit, professional and community-based arts, culture and heritage organizations in Mississauga. This grant supports the development of exemplary arts, culture programs and services with the intent to improve participation, understanding and appreciation of arts, culture and heritage for residents of Mississauga. This program provides annual and multi-year grants to Mississauga-based, not-for-profit community groups to deliver programs and services that keep Mississauga residents active, healthy and engaged in their communities. The program aligns with the strategic priorities of the Recreation and Parks, Forestry and Environment Divisions. Eligible community groups include sports organizations, groups focused on youth, older adults, outdoor recreation, adaptive and inclusive recreation, and more. Cultural traditions and celebrations are important to Mississauga residents and visitors. This program issues funding to offset expenses associated with providing arts, heritage and cultural festivals/celebrations to Mississauga residents and visitors.

items.title: Heavy Rainfall Strands Two Teens in the Credit River Before Peel Police Marine Unit Rescue
items.summary: According to CityNews Toronto, emergency crews rescued two teenagers who became stranded in the Credit River in Mississauga on Saturday after intense rainfall caused water levels to rise quickly. A Peel Regional Police spokesperson told CityNews that the rising water left the two individuals stranded on a small area of land within the river, without a boat or personal flotation devices. The outlet reports the teens contacted police themselves after realizing they were unable to safely make their way back to shore on their own. CityNews reports members of the Peel Regional Police Marine Unit responded to the scene along with several uniformed officers, paramedics and the fire department. Police told the outlet the two males were safely assisted out of the area and declined medical attention.

items.title: Peel Police Service Board Opens September Consultation on Youth Engagement Strategy
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, the Peel Police Service Board's governance and human rights committee is hosting a community consultation session on September 15 at Peel Region headquarters to gather public feedback on the police's Youth Engagement Strategy, first launched in March 2025. Mississauga.com reports the session will open with a presentation from police outlining their preliminary youth engagement plan, after which members of the public will each get up to five minutes to make their own presentations to the committee. Police spokesperson Matt Carty told the outlet the service has a long-standing commitment to youth engagement and already runs a range of youth-focused education, prevention and mentorship initiatives, including the Youth in Policing Initiative, G1/G2 Driving, Boys 2 Men, Young Women's Mentorship and partnerships through ProAction Cops and Kids. In an email to Metroland Media cited by Mississauga.com, Carty said the current consultation process is meant to help inform the ongoing evolution of the strategy and support development of a more coordinated youth services model that strengthens how the service engages and supports young people. Mississauga.com notes the strategy has been evolving since its 2025 launch, with police framing the fall consultation as a key step toward shaping that more coordinated approach going forward.

items.title: Peel Police Data Shows Over 300 Vehicle Thefts Across Mississauga and Brampton in a Single Month
items.summary: According to INsauga, Peel Regional Police data shows more than 300 vehicles were reported stolen across Mississauga and Brampton over the past month. INsauga reports the count covers the 31-day period from July 22 to August 22, during which 304 vehicle thefts were recorded across the two cities. Of those, the outlet reports 175 thefts occurred in Mississauga and 126 in Brampton, with three additional incidents in Caledon falling under Peel police's jurisdiction. INsauga notes this report differs from some previous releases in that Peel Regional Police did not provide an updated breakdown showing how many of the cases had been solved, remained under investigation or were considered unsolved. The absence of that breakdown, according to the outlet, leaves residents without a clear picture of how much progress investigators have made on any of the reported thefts.

items.title: Culham Trail Upgrade and New Port Credit Pedestrian Bridge Get $8.7 Million Federal Boost
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, the federal government's Active Transportation Fund is providing $8.7 million to support two major local projects, upgrades to the Culham Trail and construction of a new pedestrian and cycling bridge in Port Credit. The city says the Culham Trail, which stretches through Erindale Park and Riverwood and draws more than 500,000 visitors a year, will see nearly four kilometres of the multi-use recreational trail modernized, along with enhanced flood protection and added amenities such as new seating, an outlook viewing area, a bike share system, upgraded signage and landscaping. According to the city, a new 65-metre bridge designed exclusively for pedestrians and cyclists will span the Credit River between Port Credit Memorial Park and the Port Credit Royal Canadian Legion, north of Lakeshore Road, linking Port Credit and the GO Station with the Mineola West neighbourhood. The city says the bridge was identified as a priority through the Lakeshore Corridor Transportation Improvements study and advances the broader Lakeshore Connecting Communities Master Plan for walking, cycling and access to destinations along the waterfront. Together, the city reports, the two projects are meant to improve connections across Mississauga and make active transportation options easier for residents to choose.
